comparisons.label: value-dependent (θ: condition 2 only); value-dependent (η: condition 1 only)

DECISIONS: Sets: all sets of 1-3 inputs, by size then lexicographically (itertools.combinations); Markov input j is the token at lag j+1, parity input j is bit j.

Cell weights are normalised to sum 1 within each table (as projection_information does). Cells of zero weight (empty probe cells) are kept with weight 0, which is equivalent to projection_information dropping them.

Logistic fits replicate projection_information's damped Newton (gradient tolerance 1e-12, ridge 1e-12, at most 100 iterations, the same backtracking rule) but start from a warm start when it has a lower loss than beta = 0: the Walsh coefficients of the clipped logit restricted to the model's columns (hi model, and the lo model at the marginal references), or the hi solution without chi_A (lo model at the conditional references). A warm-started fit that has not converged (gradient test or a full step improving by < 1e-16) within 50 iterations is redone from beta = 0 with the 100-iteration limit, as projection_information does (on pilot data a warm start of a lo model stalled where beta = 0 converges). When the backtracking finds no decrease down to a <= 1e-8 the batched fit stops. Every fit not converged by then (iteration limit or failed backtracking) is redone with projection_information's own algorithm (tycho.ri.cells._weighted_logistic_loss from beta = 0) and the lower loss is kept; the counts are stored per object (fit_stats) and reported per region (independent verification, 14 Nov 2026: a near-singular Hessian had stalled a fit at a non-optimal point). At the marginal references the hi model is saturated and its minimum, sum_x w H(t_x), is computed in closed form.

Sampled theta_M_D and theta_C_D: the runner stores per-pattern probe counts (probe seed (seed, 'ri', step)), not sampled values. Stage 1 computes them with the exact-value code using the probe counts as cell weights. IC-2(a) recomputes them independently for 5 % of (run, checkpoint) pairs from the probe rows themselves (rows rebuilt from the counts) with cell_stats + projection_information, and requires agreement to 1e-9. The 5 % are ceil(0.05 * n_checkpoints) checkpoints per run (3 of 60), drawn with a generator seeded from (20261114, object id). IC-2(a) also regenerates the counts from the probe seed and requires them to equal the stored counts (an extra check, not in §3).

Losses are tycho.tasks.patterns.binary_losses of the stored float64 log-odds (KL from truth and squared error); for parity the KL equals the log-loss of the true label and the squared error its Brier score (§2).
Regions are those of §2: 'markov-v2' and 'parity-corr' (k = 2 and 3 together; configs/sky_v2a.yaml splits it into parity-corr-k2 and parity-corr-k3). They group IC-1's sample and IC-2(b)'s pooling.

IC-1: ceil(5 %) of the done objects of each §2 region (at least one per region), drawn with seed 20261114; each is replayed with tycho.train.run_object (spec rebuilt from the manifest and the region's train settings in configs/sky_v2a.yaml, its object id checked; RIConfig from the region's ri with enabled=True; torch with one thread, as survey workers) and compared bit for bit on every light-curve key except wall_s, and on the pattern arrays steps, logodds and counts.

IC-2(b) pools all done runs of a region (IC-5 failures included) and all checkpoints, step 0 included. The share within 0.002 nats is reported per configuration (Markov: couplings x context; parity: k x rho).

IC-3: for each chain run, the corpus is regenerated with make_task(...)._corpus; TV = 1/2 sum |pmf_D - window frequency| over its training windows; the transition check uses the binomial SE of p*: |k/n - p*| <= 5 sqrt(p*(1 - p*)/n) for every window seen >= 1,000 times. The exact pmf and p* are recomputed from the couplings and compared with the stored ones.

IC-4 compares M_D with M_U and C_D with C_U for theta and both eta values at every set and checkpoint of the iid Markov runs and the parity rho = 0 runs; the local_ri check runs at every set and checkpoint of every run, on the table P(x_A, yhat) = CellStats(counts = D marginal, sums = D marginal of pmf*m).table().

IC-5: the parity prediction is output 1 iff log-odds > 0 (argmax, ties to class 0); 'Markov runs' and 'parity runs' in the pass-rate rule are all runs of each kind in the manifest; a run that did not finish, or whose stage 1 failed, counts as failing.
Support (for 'spurious'): Markov, the union of the lags of every planted coupling with beta != 0 (4-lag couplings included), as inputs lag - 1; parity, the planted set task_cfg['support'].
Windows use the KL loss under D for the primary and the squared-error outcomes alike (T1: the run's own loss_D; T2: the 'with' network's KL loss under D_with).

Spearman: average ranks, ties are exact floating-point equality (no rounding). rho = 0 when the predictor is constant (§4), and also when the outcome is constant or a configuration has fewer than 2 points (in a resample, possibly none); none of these occurred unless reported under 'degenerate'.

Bootstrap: for each family (T1 Markov, T1 parity, T2) a fresh numpy default_rng(20261114) draws a B x n_seeds matrix of seed indices; the same resamples serve the four references and both eta values of the family. Seed labels are the sorted distinct seeds of the family's done runs. A resampled seed contributes all window points of its (IC-5-passing) run in every configuration, or of both twins of its pair; resampled duplicates enter the Spearman as tied copies (weighted mid-ranks, weighted Pearson of ranks). Bootstrap SD is the sample SD (ddof = 1) of Delta*, the CI the 2.5 and 97.5 % percentiles.

Configurations dropped from rho-bar (fewer than --min-seeds seeds passing IC-5 with at least one window point) are dropped from every resample too. A comparison with no configuration left has Delta = NaN, p = 1 in Holm (the family stays at 12), and is labelled 'not computable'.

Labels per link L: win = conditions 1, 2 and 3 for L; value-dependent = exactly one of conditions 1 and 2 holds for L; outcome-dependent = 1 and 2 hold for L but not 3. Delta = 0 favours neither link.

Secondary statistics: the pooled Spearman uses the points of the configurations that enter rho-bar; the seed-level statistic is the unweighted mean over all (configuration, checkpoint) cells with >= 3 seeds whose window contains the checkpoint; the secondary T1 predictor (all spurious sets, singletons included) and the squared-error outcome are reported as point estimates.

T2: a twin pair needs both objects done and both passing IC-5; its outcome uses binary losses with p_true = sigmoid(log-odds of the 'with' network). The identifiability residual variance is computed from the exact stationary pmf of the 'with' language (markov_window_pmf of its conditional table; uniform for iid), which is also checked against the stored pmf_D.

Q1: last checkpoint; the predictions are scored on the pooled runs (chain Markov and parity rho in {0.5, 0.8}, passing IC-5) and also reported per configs/sky_v2a.yaml region; 'smaller in total' = sum over runs of the C_D count < that of the M_D count; eta presence uses the bounded value.

Q2: all runs passing IC-5 (both regions, both contexts, every rho), sets with |A| >= 2, every checkpoint including step 0. Bins: saturation [0, 0.5, 0.74, 0.9, 0.99, 1], lower-order energy [0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1, inf). 'Per run' = number of C_D divergences (bounded value) / number of runs of the group, both contexts; 'more' is strict (equal rates do not confirm the prediction).
Q3: consecutive = adjacent checkpoints of the run's grid, step 0 excluded; shares are over seeds passing IC-5.

Q4: pairs (couplings, seed) with both runs done and passing IC-5; ties (difference exactly 0) dropped; one-sided binomial sign test, p = P(Bin(n_pos + n_neg, 1/2) >= n_pos); the eta link is scored with the bounded value, the Gaussian value is reported.

Q5 (exploratory): last checkpoint of every run passing IC-5; each link (theta, eta bounded, eta Gaussian) ranks the sets by its C_D value (ties by set order); a logistic model with an intercept and chi_A of the top K sets is fitted to the network's clipped soft output under D (weighted, soft targets) and scored by E_S KL(p_net || q) (and E_D).
